recent_posts.title: Tokenmaxxing: are we measuring AI productivity or just rewarding token burn?
recent_posts.summary: Tokenmaxxing is an emerging workplace trend where organizations track AI token consumption as a proxy for AI adoption, sometimes via internal leaderboards. The author argues this mirrors the flawed practice of measuring developers by lines of code — it captures activity but not impact. Token usage can't distinguish between genuinely productive AI workflows and wasteful prompt spam. Goodhart's Law applies: once token counts become a target, people optimize for tokens rather than outcomes. Better metrics would focus on cycle time, defect rates, incident reduction, and reusable agent workflows. While heavy AI experimentation has value during a platform shift, the best teams will be those that convert token spend into repeatable, measurable leverage.

recent_posts.title: Google’s "Jetski" Leaderboard: Brin Pushes DeepMind to Beat Claude at Coding
recent_posts.summary: Sergey Brin is reportedly pushing Google DeepMind to close the coding performance gap with Anthropic's Claude by forming a dedicated internal strike team led by Sebastian Borgeaud. DeepMind researchers internally rate Claude's code-writing above Gemini's. Google engineers are being required to use internal AI agent tools on complex tasks, with usage tracked on an internal leaderboard called 'Jetski.' The post frames this less as a model competition and more as an organizational systems story — where agent usage becomes a KPI, shifting engineering work from writing code to verifying it, and the real bottleneck becomes specifications and regression control rather than token generation.

recent_posts.title: Separating reasoning from execution in AI agents
recent_posts.summary: Octopal is a local AI agent runtime that separates reasoning from execution by using a persistent coordinator (Octo) that plans and decides, but never directly executes actions. Instead, it spawns isolated, short-lived workers with limited permissions to perform actual tasks. This architecture treats AI agents as untrusted processes, containing failures and preventing prompt injection attacks from causing real damage. The project is open source and early-stage.

recent_posts.title: How to Connect Non-Anthropic Models to Claude Code with a Gateway
recent_posts.summary: Bifrost is an open-source Go-based LLM gateway that lets Claude Code route requests to non-Anthropic providers like OpenAI, Bedrock, Vertex AI, and Gemini. It exposes an Anthropic-compatible endpoint, requiring just one install command and one environment variable. Beyond routing, it offers 11-microsecond latency overhead, automatic failover, MCP Code Mode for 50%+ token reduction, four-tier budget controls, and dual-layer semantic caching with Weaviate, Redis, or Qdrant. Primarily useful for teams with compliance requirements, multi-provider needs, or cost governance goals.

recent_posts.title: This Open-Source (MIT) Pipeline Transforms Any Podcast into AI-Ready Transcripts with Speaker Diarization
recent_posts.summary: be-flow-dtd is an MIT-licensed pipeline that automates podcast processing into AI-ready transcripts with speaker identification. It combines Whisper large-v3 for transcription, Pyannote 3.1 for diarization, and ECAPA-TDNN for speaker recognition. The system handles RSS feed discovery, generates word-level timestamps, produces speaker embeddings, and optimizes GPU memory usage to run on 8GB VRAM. Output is structured JSON suitable for RAG systems, voice assistants, content analysis, and ML training datasets.

recent_posts.title: Stop Writing Fragile Prompts: Extract Structured Data from PDFs with DSPy
recent_posts.summary: DSPy replaces fragile prompt engineering with a typed programming model where you define input/output contracts (Signatures) instead of crafting prompts. Combined with CocoIndex's incremental processing engine, you can extract structured data from PDFs using vision models without OCR or regex. The tutorial demonstrates building a patient intake form parser using Pydantic schemas, DSPy's ChainOfThought module, and CocoIndex's caching and lineage tracking to export validated data to PostgreSQL with automatic updates.

recent_posts.title: From GANs to RAG – My Deep Learning Journey
recent_posts.summary: A personal learning journey through modern deep learning architectures, starting with GANs for image generation, progressing through VAEs and Transformers, exploring pretrained models like BERT and RoBERTa, and culminating in RAG systems. The project traces how these models evolved and built upon each other, creating a connected map of innovation in generative AI and sequence processing.

recent_posts.title: MCP's 1st Birthday Hackathon • hosted by Anthropic and Gradio
recent_posts.summary: Anthropic and Gradio are hosting a 17-day hackathon focused on building AI agents using Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Gradio 6. The event runs November 14-30, 2025, offering $20,000 in cash prizes plus API credits across multiple categories including productivity, multimodal, and games. Over 4,500 developers have registered to compete solo or in teams, with prizes awarded for building MCP tools and applications, plus special awards from sponsors like Modal, Blaxel, and Google Gemini.

recent_posts.title: Deploying an LLM using vLLM on Production with Kubernetes
recent_posts.summary: Deploying large language models in production requires careful consideration of storage, GPU management, and security. Key strategies include caching models with Persistent Volumes or S3 buckets to minimize downtime, using ReadWriteMany volumes for replica scaling, labeling GPU nodes for optimal workload placement, leveraging vLLM for efficiency, and implementing authentication and access control to secure inference endpoints.

recent_posts.title: Swagger MCP Adapter, connecting LLMs with REST APIs
recent_posts.summary: An open-source adapter tool that bridges LLMs with REST APIs through MCP (Model Context Protocol). It provides four key commands for API service listing, endpoint information retrieval, comprehensive documentation access, and cache performance monitoring.
